key_insight: The paper presents a probabilistic deep learning framework that forecasts Alzheimer’s disease progression over multiple future visits while explicitly quantifying both prediction and uncertainty.
engineering_relevance: It is relevant for clinical decision-support pipelines because it combines ordinal diagnosis modeling, multi-horizon trajectory generation, and uncertainty estimates that can help flag unreliable forecasts.
method: Temporal Fusion Transformer encoder with CORAL ordinal output for diagnosis prediction
Autoregressive Mixture Density Network for five-year trajectories of diagnosis, CDR-SB, MMSE orientation, and hippocampal volume
Aleatoric/epistemic uncertainty decomposition using mixture variance and a five-member bootstrap ensemble
evidence_signal: On ADNI, the model outperformed linear, recurrent, and transformer baselines for next-visit diagnosis prediction, produced near-nominal 90% credible interval coverage, and was externally evaluated on OASIS-3.
watch_item: Performance may be sensitive to class imbalance and dataset shift, especially for rare progression patterns and external-site deployment.
paper_title: Uncertainty-Aware Longitudinal Forecasting of Alzheimer's Disease Progression Using Deep Learning
